name: Transportation Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public transportation data.

entries.title: BTS Airline On-Time Performance Statistics
entries.description: Flight-level on-time arrival and departure, delay cause, cancellation, and diversion data reported by large U.S. air carriers, published by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics through TranStats.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS)

coverage.spatial: United States (domestic flights of reporting carriers)
coverage.temporal: January 1995 through August 2026 (as stated on the page)

entries.attribution: Bureau of Transportation Statistics, Airline On-Time Statistics
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page states "Data are available from January 1995 through August 2026" and documents carrier merger reporting changes. Three things come from TranStats' usual practice and weren't checked here: flight-level detail, the monthly cadence, and CSV downloads. TranStats (https://www.transtats.bts.gov/) is reachable, but several www.bts.gov pages, such as the Freight Analysis Framework, returned Access Denied to both curl and headless Chromium this session.

entries.title: BTS/FHWA Freight Analysis Framework (FAF5)
entries.description: The Freight Analysis Framework estimates U.S. freight movement among states and major metropolitan areas by all modes: tonnage, value and ton-miles by origin-destination region, commodity and mode, for a 2017 base year, recent years, forecasts to 2050 and state-level historical trends. It is built from the Commodity Flow Survey and Census international trade data, among other sources.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS), with the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA); data site developed by Oak Ridge National Laboratory

coverage.spatial: United States (FAF regions and states; flows to and from foreign regions)
coverage.temporal: 2017 base year, 2018-2024 annual estimates, 2030-2050 forecasts, 1997-2012 state historical series

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work; DOT DataHub lists FAF as "Public Domain U.S. Government")
entries.attribution: Bureau of Transportation Statistics and Federal Highway Administration, Freight Analysis Framework Version 5 (FAF5)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium) on faf.ornl.gov. The issue's URL, https://www.bts.gov/faf, still returned Akamai "Access Denied" (HTTP 403) to curl and headless Chromium. This entry points at the FAF5 data site, which the page credits to BTS and FHWA, with ORNL listed as the developer. It says "The FAF is produced by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) with support from the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA)", and "The current version of FAF5 (FAF5.7.1) provides estimates for tonnage (unit: thousand tons), value (unit: million dollars), and ton-miles ... for the base year (2017), the recent years (2018 - 2024), the forecast year estimates (2030 - 2050), and the state level historical trend estimates (1997-2012)". Downloads are zipped regional and state databases (FAF5.7.1.zip and FAF5.7.1_access.zip, the latter presumably Access databases), plus a Data Tabulation Tool, metadata and a FAF zones shapefile. The files were not downloaded, so the CSV/Access formats are inferred from the file names.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: DOT's own open data catalog lists "Freight Analysis Framework" (https://data.transportation.gov/d/6tex-3tzx, attribution "FHWA, Office of Freight Management and Operations") with licence "Public Domain U.S. Government" (terms link https://www.usa.gov/government-works). No licence statement appears on faf.ornl.gov itself, and BTS's own FAF page could not be read, so this is catalog metadata rather than a terms page (medium confidence). Also in the issue: BTS's NTAD, which has its own entry, bts-ntad.

entries.title: DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center — Alternative Fuel Stations Data
entries.description: The U.S. Department of Energy's database of public and private alternative fuel stations in the United States and Canada (EV charging, biodiesel, CNG, E85, hydrogen, LNG, propane, renewable diesel). It powers the AFDC Station Locator and is offered as a bulk download and through an API, with historical station data.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Alternative Fuels Data Center (data provided by the National Laboratory of the Rockies, NLR)

access.auth_note: Bulk download asks for name and email and acceptance of the terms (no account); the API (developer.nlr.gov) needs a free API key (DEMO_KEY works for light use)

coverage.temporal: current station list, plus a historical stations download (start year not checked)

entries.license: AFDC Data Download Terms and Conditions (Data "may be used for any purpose whatsoever"; no endorsement use of DOE/NLR names; user indemnifies DOE/NLR)
entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Energy, Alternative Fuels Data Center, Alternative Fuel Stations data
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). The page reads "To download data related to alternative fuels and advanced vehicles, follow the steps below". The dataset choices are "Alternative fuel stations", "Laws and incentives" and "Medium- and heavy-duty vehicles", with a historical stations format page; downloads require first name, last name and email, and ticking "I have read and agree to the terms and conditions". The stations field list (https://afdc.energy.gov/data_download/alt_fuel_stations_format) covers fuel_type_code (BD, CNG, ELEC, E85, HY, LNG, LPG, RD), address fields and U.S. state or "Canadian province/territory". The Developer APIs link goes to https://developer.nlr.gov/docs/transportation/alt-fuel-stations-v1/, where the API "powers the Alternative Fueling Station Locator". A DEMO_KEY call returned station_counts total 313020 (ELEC 299913 ports at 91095 stations). The last-updated endpoint returned 2026-11-01T01:52:04Z, which is the basis for "daily". The bulk file format (CSV assumed) wasn't downloaded, and API rate limits weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the "Data Download Terms and Conditions" on https://afdc.energy.gov/data_download (terms modal) say "These data and software code ("Data") are provided by the National Laboratory of the Rockies ("NLR"), which is operated by the Alliance for Energy Innovation, LLC ("Alliance"), for the U.S. Department of Energy ("DOE"), and may be used for any purpose whatsoever." DOE/NLR/Alliance names may not be used to endorse or promote, and users "AGREE TO INDEMNIFY DOE/NLR/ALLIANCE". The data are produced by a contractor-operated laboratory, so the entry quotes these terms rather than calling them a US Gov public-domain work.

entries.title: EUROCONTROL Aviation Data Repository for Research (ADRR)
entries.description: EUROCONTROL's archive of detailed European air-traffic data for research: flight details, planned and actual flight trajectories, airspace structure and route network information for commercial flights operating in and over Europe. Free after registration, for research and development use only.
entries.publisher: EUROCONTROL (European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation)

access.auth_note: Free OneSky Online account (academic or professional email), then a vetted subscription request to the ADRR tool, and individual acceptance of the ADRR Terms of Use

coverage.spatial: Europe (commercial flights operating in and over Europe)
coverage.temporal: 2015-2025 (complete by January 2027, per EUROCONTROL), with a 12-month release delay

entries.license: EUROCONTROL ADRR Terms of Use (free, research and development use only; no commercial use, no redistribution or public display; signed by each user)
entries.attribution: "This document/R&D product has been created with or contains elements of Aviation Data Repository for Research made available by EUROCONTROL." (legend required by the Terms of Use, Article 6)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. The issue's URL, https://www.eurocontrol.int/dashboard/rnd-data-archive, redirects to https://www.eurocontrol.int/dashboard/aviation-data-research, which is catalogued here. The page reads "Aviation Data Repository for Research (ADRR)", "A huge archive of real-life, quality data", and offers "detailed flight information, flight trajectories (planned and actual), airspace structure, and route network information". It announces the move from 4 to 12 months of coverage a year and a release delay cut "from 24 to 12 months. From October 2026, the ADRR provides access to more than 100 million flight records, and by January 2027 will be covering every month from 2015 to 2025." A structure guide and sample dataset are dated 14 October 2026. Access: "The ADRR tool is open for all R&D use", via registration with OneSky Online, a subscription request that "will be vetted", then downloading, which is "simple (and free)". EUROCONTROL is an intergovernmental organisation, not an EU body; regional-bloc is the closest scope in the schema. The page also points to EUROCONTROL's general public data (https://www.eurocontrol.int/our-data, ansperformance.eu), which is not covered by this entry. File formats weren't checked (no account was used), so format is empty, and the monthly cadence is inferred from the "nearly one million flights per month" expansion.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the ADRR Terms of Use PDF (https://www.eurocontrol.int/sites/default/files/2025-04/eurocontol-aviation-data-repository-research-terms-of-use.pdf, FNI Doc24 v11 April 2025) grant "a non-exclusive, restricted, fully paid-up, royalty-free, revocable, non-sublicenseable, and non-transferable right to use" the ADRR "exclusively for R&D purposes". Users "shall not share or distribute the Aviation Data Repository for Research", shall not "display" it on any public site, and shall not "use the Aviation Data Repository for Research for commercial purposes". The data "are provided free of charge". Note that the Terms of Use still describe "four non-consecutive calendar months each year", which predates the 12-month expansion announced on the page.

entries.title: Eurostat Transport Database
entries.description: Eurostat's official EU transport statistics — road, rail, air, maritime, and inland waterway transport of passengers and goods, transport infrastructure and equipment, and road safety — harmonised across EU member states.

coverage.spatial: EU member states (plus some EFTA and candidate countries)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Eurostat copyright notice and free re-use of data)
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (page title "Database - Transport - Eurostat"). Eurostat's copyright notice (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice) licenses its content under CC BY 4.0. Transport tables range from quarterly to annual, so cadence is recorded as irregular for the collection. The modes in the description reflect Eurostat's usual transport tables and weren't checked dataset by dataset.

entries.title: FHWA Highway Statistics Series
entries.description: The Federal Highway Administration's annual reports of analyzed statistics on motor fuel, motor vehicle registrations, driver licenses, highway user taxation, highway mileage, travel, and highway finance, published since 1945.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Highway Administration (FHWA)
entries.attribution: Federal Highway Administration, Highway Statistics Series
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page describes "annual reports containing analyzed statistical information on motor fuel, motor vehicle registrations, driver licenses, highway user taxation, highway mileage, travel, and highway finance", says it has "been published annually since 1945", and lists editions through Highway Statistics 2024. The table formats are assumed and weren't checked.

entries.title: FRA Railroad Safety Data
entries.description: The Federal Railroad Administration's railroad safety data — train accidents, highway-rail grade crossing incidents and inventory, casualties, trespasser data, and operational data — as reports and full downloadable datasets.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Railroad Administration (FRA)
entries.attribution: Federal Railroad Administration, Office of Railroad Safety
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 ("Last update: Friday, October 30, 2026"). The page announces a new FRA safety data page, released in December 2024, with "reports, full datasets, and PDF reports for train accident, highway-rail crossing incident, highway-rail crossing inventory, casualty, and operational data". It lists Full Datasets and Data Downloads for each category. The FRA main site (railroads.dot.gov) returned 403 to curl. The monthly cadence and the csv format are assumed and weren't checked. A steward may want to repoint canonical_url to the new safety data page.

entries.title: International Transport Forum (ITF) Transport Statistics
entries.description: The International Transport Forum's transport statistics, published through the OECD Data Explorer: annual transport trends (freight, passenger, container, infrastructure length, road fatalities), short-term transport indicators, transport performance indicators, and infrastructure investment and maintenance spending, collected from transport ministries and statistical offices of ITF member countries.
entries.publisher: International Transport Forum (ITF) at the OECD

coverage.temporal: 1970-present for annual transport trends; varies by dataset

entries.license: unverified — the OECD terms page (oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html) and itf-oecd.org were behind a Cloudflare bot challenge and could not be read
entries.attribution: International Transport Forum (ITF), Transport statistics (OECD Data Explorer)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl; the Data Explorer is a JavaScript app and was read in headless Chromium). ITF's own site, https://www.itf-oecd.org/, returned a Cloudflare "Performing security verification" page (HTTP 403) to curl and headless Chromium, so this entry points at the OECD Data Explorer. With the Topic facet set to Transport it reports "22 datasets found": "Short term transport indicators" (7), "Annual transport trends" (6), "Infrastructure investment and maintenance spending" (1) and "Transport performance indicators" (8). The SDMX API (https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/) lists 22 dataflows under agency OECD.ITF, for example DSD_TRENDS@DF_TRENDS "Annual transport trends", DSD_ST@DF_STFAT "Fatalities" and DSD_INFRINV@DF_INFRINV. The Annual transport trends description says "Data are published annually on 31 October. Data series start in 1970 and continue until the current year-1". Whether the 31 October 2026 release had loaded wasn't checked. The topic count matched the OECD.ITF dataflow count, but I did not confirm that every Transport-topic dataset is ITF's. Formats are taken from the Data Explorer's usual download and API options and weren't tested.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: not verified. The Data Explorer's terms link (https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html) and ITF's site were both blocked as above, so no licence is asserted.

entries.title: NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)
entries.description: A nationwide census of fatal U.S. motor vehicle crashes: every crash on a public trafficway resulting in a death within 30 days, with more than 100 coded data elements describing the crash, vehicles, and people involved.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA)

coverage.spatial: United States (50 states, DC, Puerto Rico)

entries.attribution: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31 in headless Chromium on the DOT DataHub. The URL redirects to /Automobiles/Fatality-Analysis-Reporting-System-FARS-/mzrg-xkip/about_data. The page describes a crash qualifying when it "must involve a motor vehicle traveling a traffic-way customarily open to the public and resulting in the death of a person ... within 30 days", and "Each crash has more than 100 coded data elements". DOT DataHub also lists a FARS online query tool (d/vzqv-j5g4) and FTP raw data (d/kcpj-k9k9). NHTSA's own FARS page (www.nhtsa.gov) returned Access Denied to curl and headless Chromium this session, which is why this entry points at DataHub. Not checked: the 1975 start year, the Puerto Rico coverage, and the formats.

entries.title: NTSB Aviation Accident Database
entries.description: The National Transportation Safety Board's database of civil aviation accidents and selected incidents in the United States, its territories, and international waters since 1962, including foreign investigations the NTSB took part in.

coverage.spatial: United States, territories and possessions, and international waters

entries.attribution: National Transportation Safety Board, Aviation Accident Database
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page says "The NTSB aviation accident database contains civil aviation accidents and selected incidents that occurred from 1962 to present within the United States, its territories and possessions, and in international waters." NTSB's newer CAROL search lives at data.ntsb.gov, which redirects to my.ntsb.gov/basic. The download formats are assumed from NTSB's usual distribution and weren't checked. Records are added as investigations progress, so cadence is event.

entries.title: UK Road Traffic Statistics (Department for Transport)
entries.description: The Department for Transport's road traffic estimates for Great Britain — vehicle miles by vehicle type and road class, and street-level annual average daily flows and raw counts at count points — with downloads and an API.

coverage.spatial: Great Britain (regions, local authorities, count points)
coverage.temporal: 1993-present (national time series shown on the site)

entries.license: OGL-UK-3.0 (Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated)
entries.attribution: Department for Transport, Road traffic statistics
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page shows a national time series back to 1993 and offers downloads of "street-level traffic figures for all regions, local authorities and count point locations", including annual average daily flow (overall and by direction) and raw counts. It links an API and states "All content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated". Coverage is Great Britain, not Northern Ireland. Two things come from DfT's usual practice and weren't checked: the annual cadence and the csv format. The DfT publisher name is taken from the service's own branding.

entries.title: UNCTADstat
entries.description: UN Trade and Development's statistical database covering maritime transport, merchant fleets, liner shipping connectivity, and freight volumes alongside its broader trade and economy indicators.
entries.publisher: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)
entries.notes: Verified reachable this session (HTTP 200). ITF-OECD (International Transport Forum), the other natural international transport-statistics body, returned a Cloudflare bot-challenge on direct fetch — same block class as almanac-template#2. Seeded as this vertical's first international (non-US) source per operator request to seed the new verticals international-first.

entries.title: UNECE Transport Statistics Database
entries.description: The UN Economic Commission for Europe's transport tables in its statistical database: road safety (fatalities, injuries and accidents by many breakdowns), road traffic, road vehicle fleet, rail traffic and vehicles, inland waterway traffic and vessels, oil pipeline transport and transport infrastructure across the UNECE region.
entries.publisher: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE), Statistical Division

coverage.spatial: UNECE member states (Europe, North America, Central Asia, Caucasus; 56 countries in the road safety tables)

entries.license: UNECE Statistical Database terms of use (free to copy, reproduce and redistribute for commercial and non-commercial purposes, provided UNECE is acknowledged as the source)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). The issue's URL, https://unece.org/transport/statistics, returned a Cloudflare block ("Sorry, you have been blocked") to curl and headless Chromium. This entry catalogues the UNECE Statistical Database on w3.unece.org, which the UNECE Data Portal (https://w3.unece.org/PXWeb/en) links as "Transport data tables". The Transport folder lists Inland waterway traffic, Inland waterway vessels, Oil pipeline transport, "Railway employment (discontinued)", "Railway safety (discontinued)", Railway traffic, Railway vehicles, Road safety, Road traffic, Road vehicle fleet and Transport infrastructure. The PXWeb API (https://w3.unece.org/PXWeb2015/api/v1/en/STAT/40-TRTRANS) answered with JSON. The road safety tables show updated 2026-10-20, and "Road traffic fatalities and injuries, rate per million inhabitants..." covers 56 countries. The portal banner says "Economic statistics indicators have not been updated since 1 May 2026 due to database restructuring", which refers to the economic tables, not transport. The About page says the data "are compiled by the Statistical Division from a range of official national and international sources". The portal also links a transport statistics infocard and city-level public transport data (stats.unece.org), which weren't checked. Download formats beyond PX and the JSON API weren't tested.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the database's "Copyright notice and terms of use" (https://w3.unece.org/PXWeb/Static/Copyright_notice.html) reads "Copyright © United Nations. All rights reserved. The data in the UNECE Statistical Database are available free of charge. Users are free to copy, reproduce and redistribute the data for both commercial and non-commercial purposes, provided UNECE is acknowledged as the source."

entries.title: U.S. DOT Open Data Portal (data.transportation.gov)
entries.description: The Department of Transportation's open data catalog, hosting datasets from DOT operating administrations — border crossings, vehicle recalls, safety, and more — with Socrata-based APIs and downloads.
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page shows featured datasets (border crossing data, Takata recall priority groups) and links to the Socrata Terms of Use. It is a portal, not one dataset, so it's cataloged as a gateway; individual DOT datasets deserve their own entries. Some DOT bureau sites returned Access Denied to both curl and headless Chromium this session (NHTSA FARS, the FTA National Transit Database, BTS freight pages), and this portal may be the most reliable programmatic route to some of their data. The license is marked dataset-dependent because individual datasets can carry their own terms.
